quotes.text: France titres-restaurant is in private preview.
Make sure the location’s `fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments` capability status is `active` before accepting payments.
Stripe resolves the SIRET from the payment location at confirmation, not at PaymentIntent creation.
Pass this location ID in `payment_details[location]` when creating the PaymentIntent in the same sandbox.

French meal vouchers require the CVC on the first payment before they can be reused for future payments without a CVC.

findings: The November full guide adds an email access request and keeps private preview. It remains Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner only; the separate overview scopes Swile to an eligible Mastercard path, apart from this integration (old raw lines 8-17 and new raw lines 9-25; related overview lines 78-91).

The related November setup API requires CNTR licensing and issuer agreements for each issuer intended, describes each PaymentLocation as a physical branch mapped to one SIRET, and requires active `fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments`, apart from creation/pending or issuer-list updates (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:5-13,51-53,96-112,137-172,192-198`).

Source lines 19–27 and voucher concept lines 51–54 retain the May literal `payment_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][siret]` (old raw lines 19-43). The November overview still gives the literal, successfully provisioned SIRET path for Intent creation, so retain that source's wording as dated and do not infer universal removal or compatibility. The November acceptance guide's preview route uses the PaymentLocation ID in `payment_details[location]` plus `payment_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible` and requires the per-location capability to be active (new raw lines 25-48, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:119-129`). Add reciprocal version and branch-binding warnings in the overview and voucher concept. The overview separately says Stripe never retries the voucher payment as a normal card payment or vice versa. An eligibility parameter alone does not document automatic retry or fallback.

For an Intent that references a Payment Location, Stripe resolves that existing location's stored SIRET at confirmation. If the stored SIRET changes before confirmation, the new value applies, and already-confirmed payments are unaffected (new raw lines 58-74). The Dashboard guide says restaurant name and SIRET cannot be modified after creation in that workflow, while providing a Payment Location ID on verified onboarding (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-2026-11-07.md:25-51`). Scope the concept's blanket immutability at line 37. The preview setup API defaults to blocking sensitive edits such as SIRET or address; an acknowledged edit with `onboarding_data_update_acknowledged=true` triggers re-onboarding and changes capability to pending, so acceptance pauses until it is active again (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:192-198,285-310`). This timing rule does not imply that payment can proceed during the pending period.

Source lines 33–39 and voucher concept line 72 currently present May's raw test SIRET values as the test path. Keep the May provisioned/invalid SIRET test strings dated (old raw lines 57-70). The November guide keeps the Bimpli with Conecs card but tells readers to use the onboarded PaymentLocation ID from the same sandbox (new raw lines 101-109). The separate API setup guide ties the test SIRET and postal-code fixtures to simulated location onboarding, including an active `42424242842427` plus `75009` combination and pending invalid scenarios without a live Conecs call (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:342-354`). Keep the SIRET test fixture distinct from the `loc_` identifier passed to PaymentIntent.

Source line 31 has the client confirmation path but omits the earlier client-secret handoff (old raw lines 44-55, new raw lines 50-60). Separate the server-created PaymentIntent, client confirmation and redirect, and optional server retrieval of the most recent Charge. The inspection path is `latest_charge.payment_method_details.card.benefits.fr_meal_voucher.siret` with an expansion, and the API describes `latest_charge` as nullable until confirmation is attempted; confirmation can still require action or fail (new raw lines 64-99; `raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-object-2026-11-07.md:637-647`, `raw/stripe-api-payment-intents-confirm-2026-11-07.md:5-15`). This lookup is evidence of the SIRET recorded on a relevant charge, with payment success, capture and issuer settlement remaining separate.

Both acceptance captures preserve first-payment CVC before CVC-free future reuse (old raw lines 47-51 and new raw lines 52-56). Keep the optional save-during-payment branch distinct from a SetupIntent used solely for saving. November's separate save guide uses `setup_details` with the location and eligibility parameter, client `confirmSetup`, and later on-session EUR PaymentIntent with the Customer and PaymentMethod IDs and `payment_details` (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-saving-payment-details-2026-11-07.md:25-59`). Do not expand the CVC statement into arbitrary off-session reuse.

Table alignment, Payment Element quickstart link target, consolidated Elements heading, and wording are presentational or navigation edits. Diff line 90 joins the old invalid-SIRET row to new SIRET-inspection prose; both pinned raws show the boundaries separately.

answers.Q1: The November capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/accept-a-payment documents private-preview EUR acceptance for Bimpli, Pluxee and Up Déjeuner, with Stripe preview version `2026-05-27.preview` or later and an active `fr_meal_vouchers_conecs_payments` capability on the Payment Location (new raw lines 9-39). The setup API separately requires CNTR licensing and agreements with each issuer the merchant wants to support. A pending location request and issuer-list updates are distinct from activation (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:5-13,96-112,165-172,192-198`). The server creates the PaymentIntent with the branch's PaymentLocation ID in `payment_details[location]` and `payment_details[benefit][fr_meal_voucher][enabled]=if_payment_method_is_eligible`, then returns the client secret. The client confirms using Payment Element and a return URL. If the referenced location's stored SIRET changed between creation and confirmation, Stripe uses the updated SIRET. Already-confirmed payments are unaffected. To inspect it later, expand the Intent's `latest_charge` and read `payment_method_details.card.benefits.fr_meal_voucher.siret` on that Charge (new raw lines 35-99). Neither a returned client secret nor a redirect proves successful payment or settlement. The May capture and source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-payment.md instead pass a provisioned branch SIRET directly and use literal SIRET test values, with `42424242424242` representing a provisioned test SIRET and `00000000000000` an invalid SIRET. Both captures retain the first-payment CVC condition for reuse and the Payment Element handoff (old raw lines 19-70 and new raw lines 50-60). The November test retains the Bimpli with Conecs card and uses the onboarded PaymentLocation ID from the same sandbox (new raw lines 101-109).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/meal-vouchers/fr-meal-vouchers/accept-a-payment, the substantive November changes are the `2026-05-27.preview` version floor, active capability prerequisite, PaymentLocation and conditional enablement in place of a directly passed SIRET, confirmation-time lookup, optional Charge inspection, and same-sandbox location testing (old raw lines 19-43 and old raw lines 57-70, new raw lines 25-50 and new raw lines 58-109). The email waitlist is a request route for the existing private preview (old raw lines 8-10 and new raw lines 9-23). Heading consolidation, a changed quickstart link and table formatting are presentation/navigation. Date the May Elements request and literal test SIRETs in source-stripe-fr-meal-vouchers-accept-payment.md and add reciprocal warnings to the overview's literal-SIRET path and voucher concept (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-2026-11-07.md:119-129`). Dashboard onboarding exposes a Payment Location ID and keeps restaurant name and SIRET immutable in that UI. The preview setup API blocks sensitive SIRET/address edits by default. An acknowledged edit triggers re-onboarding, moves the capability to pending and pauses acceptance until reactivation (`raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-2026-11-07.md:25-51`, `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-set-up-restaurant-api-2026-11-07.md:192-198,285-310`). Keep conditional voucher opt-in separate from automatic retry as a regular card, and first-payment CVC and on-session reuse separate from SetupIntent no-charge saving. Keep server PaymentIntent creation and charge inspection distinct from client confirmation and redirect (old raw lines 44-55, new raw lines 50-99; `raw/stripe-payments-meal-vouchers-fr-meal-vouchers-saving-payment-details-2026-11-07.md:25-59`). A confirmation attempt or sandbox example does not guarantee successful authorization, capture, or issuer payout.
